requirements.text: The tests run with the language's usual test runner (node:test/Vitest, pytest, cargo test) and need no network and no model.
A unit test runs scenario 05's book-page handler alone (no whole crawl) on a saved book page.
That unit test passes a category to the handler and checks the produced item, category included.
A test runs scenario 05's whole crawl, through the library's engine, replaying the responses recorded during one earlier live run (not live, not fabricated pages).
The whole-crawl test checks that the dataset holds the expected number of books.
A test of scenario 08's AI extraction runs from the Plan learned on the earlier run, or from a scripted model reply wired so the extraction really uses it.
That AI test fails if a real model is called (no real provider reachable, frozen Plan, or an assertion on model calls).
Any test that would reach the network fails, saying which address it tried (refused or missed requests surface with their URL).

api_misuses.assumed: a context can be built by hand and its page, request, skip and push replaced with mocks
api_misuses.doc_says: AsyncCrawlContext is what a handler receives from the engine; page is a read-only property; the testing kit's AsyncTestEngine.run_handler runs a handler on a SavedResponse

api_misuses.assumed: Dataset is the record type, built with field values
api_misuses.doc_says: Dataset is a named, schema-typed collection; the record is the scenario's own model

api_misuses.assumed: mocking connect and start_crawl tests the crawl offline
api_misuses.doc_says: no engine runs: nothing is replayed (Recording mode 'replay') and no report misses are checked; the test kit's AsyncTestEngine is the offline engine
scenario 08's main never calls export; it reads outcomes and finish(), so that assertion fails

programs.notes: All three tests replace the engine with unittest mocks: the first runs scenario 08's AI on_book (not 05's handler) on a hand-built context with no saved page (and Decimal is not imported), the second and third call scenario 08's main against a mocked Foxhound, so no recording is replayed, no Plan or model guard exists and nothing checks the book count or network misses. The file is also wrapped in Markdown fences.

api_misuses.assumed: a mock HTTP server the crawl fetches from
api_misuses.doc_says: does not exist; the testing kit has TestEngine, SavedResponse, HandlerInput and run_handler, with recordings for replay

api_misuses.assumed: settings that route fetches to a mock server and disable the model
api_misuses.doc_says: no such settings exist (ConnectOptions and ai are not even imported)

api_misuses.member: run.outcomes(...) filtered on Skipped reason model_allowance_reached
api_misuses.assumed: counting skips proves no real model was called
api_misuses.doc_says: the model-call count is the report's usage.model.calls; a frozen Plan or no Model provider makes a model call fail
invented shape; records are read from the run's Dataset or the attempt result's records(&dataset)

site_errors: saved page path is the placeholder /path/to/saved/book_page.html
expected count 10 books is a guess
programs.notes: The first test runs a whole crawl from a seed through an invented mock server instead of running the book handler alone; the second runs against an empty invented mock server, not a recorded live run; the third disables the model with an invented setting and counts allowance skips instead of using a Plan or scripted reply and asserting no model calls. Nothing names missed addresses.
